questions.question: Which of the following does NOT tell you when to change gears?

options.text: Engine speed (rpm)
Road speed (mph)
The speed of the vehicle next to you

questions.correctAnswerText: The speed of the vehicle next to you
questions.explanation: Two things tell you when to shift gears. First is engine speed (rpm). Check your vehicle's manual to learn when to shift up. Second is road speed (mph). Learn which speeds work for each gear, then watch your speedometer and shift up as needed.

questions.question: If a railroad crossing gate does not go back up after a train passes, you should:

options.text: Drive around the gate.
Wait for another vehicle to cross first to see if it is safe.
Call your dispatcher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call your dispatcher.
questions.explanation: If you are stopped at a railroad crossing and the gate will not go up after the train passes, call your dispatcher. Do not drive around the lowered gate.

questions.question: If a school bus driver needs to get off the bus to check on a waiting student, the driver should:

options.text: Leave the bus running.
Turn the bus off and take the key.
Ask a student to watch the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the bus off and take the key.
questions.explanation: If students are boarding and you cannot find a student, turn off the bus and take the key with you. Check around and under the bus for the missing student.

questions.question: A commercial motor vehicle should:

options.text: Not have a fire extinguisher unless carrying hazardous materials.
Not have a fire extinguisher unless traveling through remote areas.
Never have a fire extinguisher.
Always have at least one fire extinguisher.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always have at least one fire extinguisher.
questions.explanation: All vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. When inspecting a commercial vehicle, check for at least one fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless the vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices for when the vehicle is parked.

questions.question: In very hot weather, tire air pressure may increase.

options.text: True
False

questions.correctAnswerText: True
questions.explanation: Hot air expands, so tire pressure increases in very hot weather. Stop often to check that your tires will not blow out or catch fire.

questions.question: If federal inspectors find your vehicle unsafe, they can:

options.text: Take you to a garage to have it fixed.
Formally ask you to have problems fixed.
Call a mechanic.
Remove the vehicle from service until it is fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove the vehicle from service until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: If a federal or state inspector finds a commercial vehicle unsafe, they can remove it from service until it is fixed.

questions.question: A 10-foot load must be secured by at least ____ tie-downs.

options.text: Two
Three
Four

questions.correctAnswerText: Two
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers and trailers without sides, cargo must be tied down. Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. Always use at least two tie-downs, no matter the cargo size.

questions.question: Driving at night is:

options.text: Safer than driving during the day.
Just as safe as driving during the day.
More dangerous than driving during the day.
Not recommended.

questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous than driving during the day.
questions.explanation: Driving at night is more dangerous than driving during the day. It is harder to see hazards, headlight glare can affect vision, and more tired and impaired drivers are on the road.

questions.question: Before driving a bus, you should make sure it is safe by:

options.text: Reading the inspection report from the previous driver.
Kicking the tires.
Asking your supervisor if the bus seems safe.
Asking passengers if they feel comfortable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reading the inspection report from the previous driver.
questions.explanation: Always inspect a bus before driving it. You must read the inspection report from the previous driver. Only drive the bus if any listed defects have been fixed or do not need fixing.

questions.question: Which of the following means brakes need repair?

options.text: Brake pads are not covered in grease.
Brake pads are not covered in oil.
Brake shoes are worn very thin.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake shoes are worn very thin.
questions.explanation: When checking brakes, look for cracked drums, shoes or pads covered in oil, grease, or brake fluid, and shoes that are missing, broken, or worn dangerously thin.

questions.question: When other vehicles have trouble seeing you at dawn or dusk, how can you increase your visibility?

options.text: Turn on your four-way flashers.
Honk your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Turn on your windshield wipers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dawn, dusk, or in snow or rain, turn on your headlights. This helps other drivers see your vehicle.

questions.question: What happens if you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: You fail only that exercise.
That exercise is reset.
You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
You get an extra point against your score.

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle, you must face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. For a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly results in automatic failure of the test.

questions.question: While driving, what is permitted regarding texting?

options.text: You cannot create texts, but you can read them.
You can create texts, but you cannot read them.
You cannot create or read texts.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot create or read texts.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is not allowed. This includes typing text or reading text on an electronic device.

questions.question: A posted speed limit for cars:

options.text: Is usually safe for buses.
May be too fast for buses.
May be too slow for buses.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be too fast for buses.
questions.explanation: Speed limits for cars may be too fast for buses, especially on curves. Be extra careful when roads are wet or snowy.

questions.question: What is axle weight?

options.text: The weight that presses down on the ground from one axle
The weight of one axle
How much weight an axle can hold

questions.correctAnswerText: The weight that presses down on the ground from one axle
questions.explanation: Axle weight is the weight transmitted to the ground by one axle or set of axles.

questions.question: ____ is a thin layer of ice on road surfaces.

options.text: White ice
Black ice
Green ice

questions.correctAnswerText: Black ice
questions.explanation: Black ice is a thin, clear layer of ice. You can see the road through it, so it looks like a wet road instead of ice. Watch for black ice when roads look wet and the temperature is around freezing.

questions.question: If your bus stalls on railroad tracks, what should you do?

options.text: Get everyone out of the bus and move far away from it.
Keep everyone in the bus and try to wave down the train.
Keep everyone in the bus and wait for help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get everyone out of the bus and move far away from it.
questions.explanation: If a bus stalls on railroad tracks, get everyone out immediately. Move away from the tracks at an angle, in the direction of any oncoming train.

questions.question: When approaching a school bus stop, the driver should:

options.text: Not use their mirrors.
Approach slowly and carefully.
Stop on the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: Always approach bus stops slowly and with caution.

questions.question: When changing lanes, turn signals:

options.text: Should not be used.
Should only be used if a vehicle is close to you.
Should always be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should always be used.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Do not assume other drivers will move just because you are signaling.

questions.question: Emergency roof hatches on a bus:

options.text: Must be closed before driving.
Can be opened to allow fresh air while driving.
Must be removed before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be opened to allow fresh air while driving.
questions.explanation: Some emergency roof hatches can be locked open to allow fresh air. However, this should not be done regularly.
